name: CONFIDeNT
aliases: CONtrol of Faecal Incontinence using Distal NeuromodulaTion
question: Does percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation improve faecal incontinence response compared with sham stimulation after conservative treatment has failed?

design.blinding: patients and outcome assessors masked; treating investigators unmasked
design.population: 227 adults with substantial faecal incontinence despite conservative treatment were randomized in 17 UK specialist hospital units.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, pragmatic superiority randomized trial
design.locator: Lancet PubMed abstract, Methods and Findings; Horrocks 2017 PubMed abstract, Background

verdictNote: The prespecified diary-defined responder comparison did not differ significantly.
takeaway: After 12 weekly treatments for faecal incontinence, percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation did not significantly increase diary-defined responders versus sham electrical stimulation (39/103 [38%] versus 32/102 [31%]; adjusted OR 1.28, 95% CI 0.72–2.28).

reports.label: Primary Lancet report
reports.citation: Knowles CH, Horrocks EJ, Bremner SA, et al. "Percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation versus sham electrical stimulation for the treatment of faecal incontinence in adults (CONFIDeNT): a double-blind, multicentre, pragmatic, parallel-group, randomised controlled trial." *Lancet.* 2015;386(10004):1640-1648. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(15)60314-2
reports.followUp: Response assessed after 12 weekly treatments during the 14-week masked trial

results.endpoint: ≥50% reduction in weekly faecal incontinence episodes
results.measure: Diary-complete responders after 12 sessions; adjusted odds ratio from intention-to-treat analysis with multiple imputation
results.note: The displayed proportions use complete bowel diaries; missing data were multiply imputed for the adjusted analysis.

harms.note: Needle-site pain accounted for four PTNS events and three sham events.

harms.label: Serious treatment-related adverse events
harms.note: One patient per group withdrew after an adverse event unrelated to treatment.

delivery.locator: Full text, Figure 3, p 17; Results, p 18
delivery.note: Twelve patients withdrew from treatment or the trial (seven PTNS, five sham). The companion NIHR HTA report (doi:10.3310/hta19770) identifies five citing weekly treatment commitments, seven withdrawing from the trial and five from treatment only.

delivery.label: PTNS and sham protocol
delivery.value: Urgent PC 34-gauge needle inserted about 2 cm deep, 5 cm cephalad to the medial malleolus and 2 cm posterior to the tibia, with sensory or motor response confirmed; 30 minutes weekly for 12 treatments. Sham needle inserted 2 mm at the same site with foot TENS at 10 Hz and 200 microseconds.

delivery.label: Treatment completion
delivery.note: 197/227 met the per-protocol definition of at least 10 treatments within 13 weeks, spaced 5–10 days apart.
delivery.locator: Full text, Figure 3, p 17; Results, p 32
